questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}z)\text{ }k \\  & =(1-2xz)\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j-{x}^{2}k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,2) & =(\,1-2(1)(2)\,)\text{ }i+2(1)\text{ }j-(1)^{2}k \\  & =-3\,i+2\,j-1\,k \\  & =⟨-3,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-3,2,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=xy-yz-xz$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,3,4).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,3,4):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-yz-xz)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-yz-xz)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy-yz-xz)\text{ }k \\  & =(y-z)\text{ }i+(x-z)\text{ }j+(-y-x)k \\ ∇\,f(2,3,4) & =(3-4)\text{ }i+(2-4)\text{ }j+(-3-2)k \\  & =-1\text{ }i-2\text{ }j-5k \\  & =⟨-1,-2,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,3,4)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,-2,-5⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ -(x-2)-2(y-3)-5(z-4) & =0 \\ -x-2y-5z+28 & =0 \\ x+2y+5z-28 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,-1,1):$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇\,f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,1,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =2x\text{ }i+8y\text{ }j+4z\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(2,1,1) & =2(2)\text{ }i+8(1)j+4(1)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i+8\,j+4\,k \\  & =⟨4,8,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇\,f(2,1,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,8,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-2)+8(y-1)+4(z-1) & =0 \\ 4x+8y+4z-20 & =0 \\ x+2y+z-5 & =0\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,-1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x)\text{ }k \\  & =(2xz+{y}^{2})\text{ }i+({z}^{2}+2yx)\text{ }j+({x}^{2}+2zy)k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,-1) & =(2(1)(-1)+{1}^{2})\text{ }i+((-1)^{2}+2(1)(1))\text{ }j+({1}^{2}+2(-1)(1))k \\  & =-\,i+3\,j-k \\  & =⟨-1,3,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ -(x-1)+3(y-1)-(z+1) & =0 \\ -x+3y-z-3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface ${x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}=17.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(2,-2,1),$ what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=17.$   

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(2,-2,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1})j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+{e}^{z-1}))k \\  & =2x{y}^{2}i+2y{x}^{2}j+{e}^{z-1}k \\ ∇f(2,-2,1) & =2(2)(-2)^{2}\text{ }i+2(-2){2}^{2}\text{ }j+{e}^{1-1}\text{ }k \\  & =16\text{ }i-16\text{ }j+\text{ }k \\  & =⟨16,\,-16,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨16,\,-16,\,1⟩.$ 

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{16}{1}=16.$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $x{y}^{2}+6=z{x}^{2}.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(-2,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x{y}^{2}+6 & =z{x}^{2} \\ x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2} & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2}$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-6.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-2,-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =({y}^{2}-2xz)\text{ }i+2xy\text{ }j-{x}^{2}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-2,-1,1) & =((-1)^{2}-2(-2)(1))\text{ }i+2(-2)(-1)\text{ }j-(-2)^{2}\text{ }k \\  & =5\,i+4j-4\,k \\  & =⟨5,4,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-2,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,4,-4⟩\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 5(x+2)+4(y+1)-4(z-1) & =0 \\ 5x+4y-4z+18 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})=1-x.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,-2,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+2{z}^{2}) & =1-x \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})+x-1 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

If we set $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})+x-1$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,-2,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})+x-1\,)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})+x-1\,)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})+x-1\,)\text{ }k \\  & =\text{ }i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})\text{ }j+4z\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+2{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(1,-2,1) & =\text{ }i+\operatorname{cos}⁡((-2)+2(1)^{2})\text{ }j+4(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡((-2)+2(1)^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =i+j+4\,k \\  & =⟨1,1,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,-2,1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨1,1,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ (x-1)+(y+2)+4(z-1) & =0 \\ x+y+4z-3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz=2+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(\frac{\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2},2),$ what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)=z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=2+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.$  

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(\frac{\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2},2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz)i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz)j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz)k \\  & =(-z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)-yz)i+(-z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)-xz)j+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xy)k \\ ∇f(\frac{\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2},2) & =(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2})-2(-\frac{\pi }{2}))\text{ }i+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2})-2(\frac{\pi }{2}))\text{ }j+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{\pi }{2})(-\frac{\pi }{2}))\text{ }k \\  & =\pi \text{ }i-\pi \text{ }j+(1+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4})\text{ }k \\  & =⟨\pi ,\,-\pi ,\,1+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨\pi ,\,-\pi ,\,\frac{{\pi }^{2}+4}{4}⟩.$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{\pi }{-\pi }=-1.$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,2,-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z{x}^{4}-x-2{y}^{3})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{x}^{4}-x-2{y}^{3})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{x}^{4}-x-2{y}^{3})\text{ }k \\  & =(4{x}^{3}z-1)\text{ }i-6{y}^{2}\text{ }j+{x}^{4}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-1,2,-3) & =(4(-1)^{3}(-3)-1)\text{ }i-6(2)^{2}\text{ }j+(-1)^{4}\text{ }k \\  & =11\,i-24j+k \\  & =⟨11,-24,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,2,-3)\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-2,\,z+3⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨11,-24,1⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-2,\,z+3⟩ & =0 \\ 11(x+1)-24(y-2)+(z+3) & =0 \\ 11x-24y+z+62 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z) = x^2+y^2+z^2,$ find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,-2,1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

$$
\nabla \! f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle  = 0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(x_0,y_0,z_0) =(2,-2,1)\mathbin{:}$  

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}\,i+{f}_{y}\,j+{f}_{z}\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j+2z\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(2,-2,1) & =2(2)\text{ }i+2(-2)\text{ }j+2(1)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i-4\,j+2\text{ }k \\  & =⟨4,\,-4\,,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇\,f(2,-2,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-(-2),\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,\,-4,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-2)-4(y+2)+2(z-1) & =0 \\ 4x-4y+2z-18 & =0 \\ 2x-2y+z-9 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Consider the surface $z^3y^2 =x^2-5.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to this surface at the point $(-1,2,-1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{3}{y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-5 \\ {z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z) = z^3y^2 - x^2,$ our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-5.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

$$
\nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle  = 0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,2,-1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =(-2x)\text{ }i+2{z}^{3}y\text{ }j+3{z}^{2}{y}^{2}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-1,2,-1) & =(-2)(-1)\text{ }i+2(-1)^{3}(2)\text{ }j+3(-1)^{2}(2)^{2}\text{ }k \\  & =2\,i-4j+12\,k \\  & =⟨2,-4,12⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,2,-1)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-2,\,z-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-4,12⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-2,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ 2(x+1)-4(y-2)+12(z+1) & =0 \\ 2x-4y+12z+22 & =0 \\ x-2y+6z+11 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
In this lesson, we will learn how to compute the tangent plane to the level surface $f (x, y, z) = k,$ where $k$ is a constant, at some point $\mathbf x_0 = (x_0, y_0, z_0).$ 

As an example, consider the function

$$
f(x,y,z) = x^2 +y^2+z.
$$

 

Suppose that we wish to find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=  (1,1, 2).$ 

Evaluating $f$ at the point $(1,1,2),$ we get

$$
f(x,y,z) = (1)^2 +(1)^2+2 = 4.
$$

 

So, the equation of our level surface is

$$
x^2 +y^2+z = 4.
$$

Now, to find the equation of the tangent plane to this surface at $(1,1,2),$ we can use the following result:

  *Given a hypersurface $w = f(x,y,z)$ and a point $\mathbf x_0 = (x_0,y_0,z_0)$ that lies in the domain of $f$, the gradient $\nabla \! f (\mathbf x_0)$ is normal to the tangent plane of the level surface $f (x, y, z) = k$ at the point $\mathbf x_0$*. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153845/assets/1140e80fbb2efd684311cb7625e5b0be361d6fb951036253f57b9e51234de3ee.png)

       

We can now find the equation of the tangent plane to our level surface.

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $\mathbf x_0 = (1,1,2)\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}\,i+{f}_{y}\,j+{f}_{z}\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+z)\text{ }k \\  & =2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j+k \\ ∇f(1,1,2) & =2(1)\text{ }i+2(1)\text{ }j+k \\  & =2\text{ }i+2\text{ }j+k \\  & =⟨2,\,2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally,  we write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\eqalign{
\nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle & = 0 \[3pt]
\nabla f(1,1,2) \cdot \langle x-1, \: y-1, \: z-2 \rangle & = 0 \[3pt]
\langle 2,\:2,\:1\rangle\cdot \langle x-1, y-1, z-2\rangle &= 0\[3pt]
      2(x-1)+ 2(y-1) + (z-2) & =0\
      2x +2y +z -6&=0   
}
$$
